why: THE ITALIAN RECORD (Nov 2026, the Italian beginner pass — docs/lang-decks.md). Applied by .claude/decks/italian-fix.js AFTER paradigm-fix.js; read its header first. What is here: the cards CILS A1 gains (`insert`), the cards another deck loses to it (`decks.<id>.dropDup`), the feminine adjectives that were a second card for one word (`decks.<id>.dropForm`), fields rebuilt on a card the generator wrote (`notes`), and each deck's words about itself (`decks.<id>.subtitle`, `descSub`). The folded paradigms stay in paradigm-fixes.json. NOTHING HERE IS COMPOSED: a moved card's `fields` are the card as it stood in the deck named by `from`, byte for byte; a new card's meanings are the English Wiktionary's (kaikki.org, read 2026-11-16), its forms the Wikipedia table its `why` names, and each of its sentences a Tatoeba sentence named by id in `src` (CC BY 2.0 FR).

descSub: 3039 of them, built by the same pipeline
3039 of them less the 19 that a CILS deck now carries or that were a second card for one word, built by the same pipeline
On its own it is a better first deck than any of them.

WHERE IT SITS: the shelf lists it after the six bands, and it is not harder than they are. Measured against the same subtitle frequency list, its first 300 words are about as common as the first 300 of CILS B1 (a median rank of 2,525 against 2,443) and 417 of its words are among the 5,000 commonest forms of spoken Italian, while its last 2,000 are rarer than the middle of C1. So begin it beside CILS A2, when A1 is done, rather than after C2: at a language deck's default of ten new cards a day, which is five words a day, the six bands alone take 1,431 days to reach it, and this deck takes 604. The greetings it used to hold (buongiorno, buonasera, arrivederci, salve) and seven numbers are cards of CILS A1 now.

So read the order as a rough guide rather than a ranking — the commonest expressions really are at the front, but a few further down deserve to be nearer it. THE DECK IS ALSO TIERED BY WHAT YOU CAN ALREADY READ: first the 658 expressions spelled entirely with words and forms CILS A1 shows, then those that need A2 (189), B1 (95), B2 (48), C1 (39), C2 (6) and the core vocabulary (129), and last the 208 that use a word no deck cards; inside a tier the order is still the corpus count. So this deck need not wait for the others, though the shelf lists it last: its first 658 cards can be studied beside CILS A1. At a language deck's default of ten new cards a day, which is five expressions a day, they take 132 days and the whole deck 275. Four expressions a beginner needs on the first day — per favore, mi chiamo, come stai, va bene — are cards of CILS A1 and are not here.

SO THE ORDER IS DOING THE WORK. The cards are dealt by how common the word actually is in everyday spoken Italian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles, so you meet e, non, che, di, la in the first handful and the rarest of the band at the end.

SO THE ORDER IS DOING THE WORK, and it begins by hand. The first 76 cards are the courtesies (ciao, buongiorno, grazie, prego, per favore, scusa), the words of a first exchange (io, essere, tu, mi chiamo, come stai) with the commonest function words, the other subject pronouns, ten verbs, the question words and zero to ten. After them the cards are dealt by how common the word actually is in everyday spoken Italian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles, with each closed set kept together — the days of the week from card 151, the numbers above ten from 251, the months and the seasons from 351 — look-alikes forty cards apart, and the rarest of the band at the end. The prepositions di, a, da, in and su show the forms they take with the article (del, alla, nei). THE PACE: a deck cannot set its own daily limit, and a language deck's default is ten new cards a day with both directions together, which is five words a day. At that pace the courtesies take three days, the first 76 cards sixteen, the days of the week arrive on day 31 and the whole deck takes 201 days. It is a large first deck — the band is a frequency band of about a thousand words, not a beginner's syllabus — so raise New cards a day in the deck's options to finish sooner, and study Italian — Sounds and spelling beside it from the first day.
